30: #define VP_STATE_FINISHED 2  /* the thread returned, still needs a join */

32: #define VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS  200
33: #define VP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS 5000

37: struct vp_server_s

39:   int       listenfd;
40:   pthread_t thread;
41:   int       state;
42:   bool      stopping;
43:   bool      one_shot;
44:   char      store_path[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX];

53:   .state    = VP_STATE_IDLE,

56: static pthread_mutex_t g_lock = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;

58: /* Request and response buffers are static because only one connection is
59:  * served at a time and 6KB of thread stack on this part is not free.

65: static int vp_write_all(int fd, const char *data, size_t len)
66: {
67:   size_t sent = 0;
68: 
69:   while (sent < len)
70:     {
71:       ssize_t n = write(fd, data + sent, len - sent);
72: 
73:       if (n < 0)
74:         {
75:           if (errno == EINTR)
76:             {
77:               continue;
78:             }
79: 
80:           return -errno;
81:         }
82: 
83:       if (n == 0)
84:         {
85:           return -EPIPE;
86:         }
87: 
88:       sent += (size_t)n;
89:     }

94: /****************************************************************************
95:  * Name: vp_read_request
96:  *
97:  * Description:
98:  *   Read until the headers plus the declared body have arrived, the cap is
99:  *   reached or the deadline passes.  Returns the total length, or negative on
100:  *   error.  A client that opens a connection and says nothing costs one
101:  *   timeout, not the service.
102:  *
103:  ****************************************************************************/
104: 
105: static int vp_read_request(int fd, struct vp_http_request_s *req)
106: {
107:   size_t total = 0;
108:   int waited = 0;
109: 
110:   for (; ; )
111:     {
112:       struct pollfd pfd;
113:       ssize_t n;
114:       int ret;
115: 
116:       ret = vp_http_parse(g_request, total, req);
117:       if (ret == 0)
118:         {
119:           if (req->action != VP_HTTP_ACTION_SAVE ||
120:               total >= req->header_len + req->content_length)
121:             {
122:               return (int)total;
123:             }
124:         }
125:       else if (ret != -EAGAIN)
126:         {
127:           return ret;
128:         }
129: 
130:       if (total >= sizeof(g_request) - 1)
131:         {
132:           return -E2BIG;
133:         }
134: 
135:       pfd.fd = fd;
136:       pfd.events = POLLIN;
137:       pfd.revents = 0;
138:       ret = poll(&pfd, 1, VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS);
139:       if (ret < 0)
140:         {
141:           if (errno == EINTR)
142:             {
143:               continue;
144:             }
145: 
146:           return -errno;
147:         }
148: 
149:       if (ret == 0)
150:         {
151:           waited += VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS;
152:           if (waited >= VP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS)
153:             {
154:               return -ETIMEDOUT;
155:             }
156: 
157:           continue;
158:         }
159: 
160:       n = read(fd, g_request + total, sizeof(g_request) - 1 - total);
161:       if (n < 0)
162:         {
163:           if (errno == EINTR)
164:             {
165:               continue;
166:             }
167: 
168:           return -errno;
169:         }
170: 
171:       if (n == 0)
172:         {
173:           /* Peer closed.  Whatever arrived is all there will be, so let the
174:            * parser decide between "incomplete" and "answerable".
175:            */
176: 
177:           if (vp_http_parse(g_request, total, req) == 0 &&
178:               (req->action != VP_HTTP_ACTION_SAVE ||
179:                total >= req->header_len + req->content_length))
180:             {
181:               return (int)total;
182:             }
183: 
184:           return -ECONNRESET;
185:         }
186: 
187:       total += (size_t)n;
188:     }

191: /****************************************************************************
192:  * Name: vp_handle
193:  *
194:  * Description:
195:  *   Serve one connection.  Sets *saved when credentials were persisted and
196:  *   *save_status to 0 or the negative errno of a failed save, so the caller can
197:  *   notify the application only after the socket is gone.
198:  *
199:  ****************************************************************************/

201: static void vp_handle(int fd, bool *saved, int *save_status,
202:                       uint32_t *generation)
203: {
204:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s cred;
205:   struct vp_http_request_s req;
206:   size_t len = 0;
207:   int ret;
208: 
209:   *saved = false;
210:   *save_status = 0;
211: 
212:   ret = vp_read_request(fd, &req);
213:   if (ret < 0)
214:     {
215:       if (ret == -E2BIG)
216:         {
217:           len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 431,
218:                                     "请求过大。");
219:         }
220:       else
221:         {
222:           /* Nothing usable arrived; answering a client that already gave up
223:            * is not worth a second syscall.
224:            */
225: 
226:           return;
227:         }
228:     }
229:   else if (req.action == VP_HTTP_ACTION_PAGE)
230:     {
231:       len = vp_http_form_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), NULL);
232:     }
233:   else if (req.action == VP_HTTP_ACTION_REJECT)
234:     {
235:       len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), req.status,
236:                                req.status == 404 ? "页面不存在。" :
237:                                req.status == 405 ? "不支持该请求方法。" :
238:                                req.status == 413 ? "提交内容过大。" :
239:                                req.status == 415 ? "提交格式不受支持。" :
240:                                req.status == 411 ? "缺少 Content-Length。" :
241:                                                    "请求无法解析。");
242:     }
243:   else
244:     {
245:       memset(&cred, 0, sizeof(cred));
246:       ret = vp_form_parse(g_request + req.header_len, req.content_length,
247:                           &cred);
248:       if (ret < 0)
249:         {
250:           /* No detail about which field failed and no echo of what was typed:
251:            * the notice has to be useful to the person at the phone without
252:            * repeating a passphrase back over an open network.
253:            */
254: 
255:           len = vp_http_form_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response),
256:                                   "SSID 需 1-32 字节，密码需留空或 8-63 字节，"
257:                                   "请检查后重试。");
258:           if (len > 0)
259:             {
260:               /* Reuse the form page body but answer 400, so a client that
261:                * checks the status still learns the submit failed.
262:                */
263: 
264:               len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 400,
265:                                         "SSID 需 1-32 字节，密码需留空或 "
266:                                         "8-63 字节。");
267:             }
268:         }
269:       else
270:         {
271:           cred.generation = vp_store_next_generation(g_server.store_path);
272:           ret = vp_store_save(g_server.store_path, &cred);
273:           if (ret < 0)
274:             {
275:               *saved = false;
276:               *save_status = ret;
277:               len = vp_http_status_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response), 500,
278:                                         "写入持久存储失败，凭据未保存。");
279:             }
280:           else
281:             {
282:               *saved = true;
283:               *save_status = 0;
284:               *generation = cred.generation;
285:               len = vp_http_saved_page(g_response, sizeof(g_response),
286:                                        cred.ssid, cred.generation,
287:                                        cred.open_network);
288:             }
289:         }
290:     }
291: 
292:   if (len > 0)
293:     {
294:       (void)vp_write_all(fd, g_response, len);
295:     }

298: static void *vp_thread(void *arg)
299: {
300:   (void)arg;
301: 
302:   for (; ; )
303:     {
304:       struct pollfd pfd;
305:       uint32_t generation = 0;
306:       int save_status = 0;
307:       bool saved = false;
308:       bool stopping;
309:       int fd;
310:       int ret;
311: 
312:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
313:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
314:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
315:       if (stopping)
316:         {
317:           break;
318:         }
319: 
320:       pfd.fd = g_server.listenfd;
321:       pfd.events = POLLIN;
322:       pfd.revents = 0;
323: 
324:       /* Polling rather than blocking in accept(): stop() then needs no signal
325:        * and no socket shutdown trick that may or may not wake accept on a
326:        * given stack.
327:        *
328:        * This requires CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG on NuttX, which the Kconfig
329:        * depends on.  Without it TCP_BACKLOG events never fire, POLLIN on a
330:        * listening socket is unreachable, and accept() blocks with no timeout
331:        * at all -- measured on the board as a service that reported
332:        * "listening" and then answered nothing.
333:        */
334: 
335:       ret = poll(&pfd, 1, VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS);
336:       if (ret < 0)
337:         {
338:           if (errno == EINTR)
339:             {
340:               continue;
341:             }
342: 
343:           break;
344:         }
345: 
346:       if (ret == 0)
347:         {
348:           continue;
349:         }
350: 
351:       fd = accept(g_server.listenfd, NULL, NULL);
352:       if (fd < 0)
353:         {
354:           if (errno == EINTR || errno == ECONNABORTED)
355:             {
356:               continue;
357:             }
358: 
359:           break;
360:         }
361: 
362:       vp_handle(fd, &saved, &save_status, &generation);
363: 
364:       /* Close before notifying.  The application is expected to leave SoftAP
365:        * from the callback, and doing that with the response still in flight is
366:        * what makes a successful save look like a failed submit on the phone.
367:        */
368: 
369:       shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR);
370:       close(fd);
371: 
372:       if (saved)
373:         {
374:           pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
375:           g_server.generation = generation;
376:           pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
377:         }
378: 
379:       if (saved || save_status < 0)
380:         {
381:           if (g_server.on_saved != NULL)
382:             {
383:               g_server.on_saved(save_status, generation, g_server.cb_arg);
384:             }
385:         }
386: 
387:       if (saved && g_server.one_shot)
388:         {
389:           break;
390:         }
391: 
392:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
393:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
394:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
395:       if (stopping)
396:         {
397:           break;
398:         }
399:     }
400: 
401:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
402:   if (g_server.listenfd >= 0)
403:     {
404:       close(g_server.listenfd);
405:       g_server.listenfd = -1;
406:     }
407: 
408:   g_server.state = VP_STATE_FINISHED;
409:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
410:   return NULL;
411: }

415: static void vp_reap_locked(void)
416: {
417:   if (g_server.state == VP_STATE_FINISHED)

422:       pthread_join(thread, NULL);
423:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
424:       g_server.state = VP_STATE_IDLE;
425:     }

16: #define VP_OFF_MAGIC     0
17: #define VP_OFF_VERSION   4
18: #define VP_OFF_FLAGS     6
19: #define VP_OFF_GEN       8
20: #define VP_OFF_SSID_LEN  12

29: uint32_t vp_crc32(const void *data, size_t len)
30: {
31:   const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)data;
32:   uint32_t crc = 0xffffffffu;
33:   size_t i;
34: 
35:   /* Bitwise rather than a table: 114 bytes twice per save is not worth 1KB of
36:    * flash on a part that is already at 90% of its region.
37:    */
38: 
39:   for (i = 0; i < len; i++)
40:     {
41:       unsigned bit;
42: 
43:       crc ^= p[i];
44:       for (bit = 0; bit < 8; bit++)
45:         {
46:           crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (0xedb88320u & (uint32_t)(-(int32_t)(crc & 1u)));
47:         }
48:     }
49: 
50:   return crc ^ 0xffffffffu;
51: }

53: static void vp_put16(uint8_t *buf, uint16_t value)
54: {
55:   buf[0] = (uint8_t)(value & 0xffu);
56:   buf[1] = (uint8_t)((value >> 8) & 0xffu);
57: }
58: 
59: static void vp_put32(uint8_t *buf, uint32_t value)
60: {
61:   buf[0] = (uint8_t)(value & 0xffu);
62:   buf[1] = (uint8_t)((value >> 8) & 0xffu);
63:   buf[2] = (uint8_t)((value >> 16) & 0xffu);
64:   buf[3] = (uint8_t)((value >> 24) & 0xffu);
65: }

68: {
69:   return (uint16_t)((uint16_t)buf[0] | (uint16_t)((uint16_t)buf[1] << 8));
70: }
71: 
72: static uint32_t vp_get32(const uint8_t *buf)
73: {
74:   return (uint32_t)buf[0] | ((uint32_t)buf[1] << 8) |
75:          ((uint32_t)buf[2] << 16) | ((uint32_t)buf[3] << 24);
76: }

90: int vp_record_encode(uint8_t *buf, size_t buflen,
91:                      const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
92: {
93:   size_t ssid_len;
94:   size_t psk_len;
95:   int ret;
96: 
97:   if (buf == NULL || cred == NULL)
98:     {

100:     }
101: 
102:   if (buflen < VP_RECORD_SIZE)
103:     {
104:       return -E2BIG;
105:     }
106: 
107:   ret = vp_credentials_validate(cred);
108:   if (ret < 0)
109:     {

111:     }

113:   ssid_len = vp_len(cred->ssid, sizeof(cred->ssid));
114:   psk_len  = vp_len(cred->password, sizeof(cred->password));
115: 
116:   memset(buf, 0, VP_RECORD_SIZE);
117:   memcpy(buf + VP_OFF_MAGIC, VP_RECORD_MAGIC, 4);
118:   vp_put16(buf + VP_OFF_VERSION, VP_RECORD_VERSION);
119:   vp_put16(buf + VP_OFF_FLAGS,
120:            cred->open_network ? VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN : 0);
121:   vp_put32(buf + VP_OFF_GEN, cred->generation);
122:   buf[VP_OFF_SSID_LEN] = (uint8_t)ssid_len;
123:   buf[VP_OFF_PSK_LEN]  = (uint8_t)psk_len;
124:   memcpy(buf + VP_OFF_SSID, cred->ssid, ssid_len);
125:   memcpy(buf + VP_OFF_PSK, cred->password, psk_len);
126:   vp_put32(buf + VP_OFF_CRC, vp_crc32(buf, VP_RECORD_SIZE - 4));
127:   return VP_RECORD_SIZE;

130: static bool vp_padding_is_zero(const uint8_t *buf, size_t offset,
131:                                size_t used, size_t field)
132: {
133:   size_t i;
134: 
135:   for (i = used; i < field; i++)
136:     {
137:       if (buf[offset + i] != 0)
138:         {
139:           return false;
140:         }
141:     }
142: 
143:   return true;

146: int vp_record_decode(const uint8_t *buf, size_t len,
147:                      struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
148: {
149:   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s parsed;
150:   size_t ssid_len;
151:   size_t psk_len;
152:   uint16_t flags;
153: 
154:   if (buf == NULL || cred == NULL)
155:     {
156:       return -EINVAL;
157:     }
158: 
159:   /* Exactly one size is legal.  A shorter file is a truncated write and a
160:    * longer one is not this format, and neither is worth guessing about.
161:    */
162: 
163:   if (len != VP_RECORD_SIZE)
164:     {
165:       return -EBADMSG;
166:     }
167: 
168:   if (memcmp(buf + VP_OFF_MAGIC, VP_RECORD_MAGIC, 4) != 0 ||
169:       vp_get16(buf + VP_OFF_VERSION) != VP_RECORD_VERSION ||
170:       buf[VP_OFF_RESERVED] != 0)
171:     {
172:       return -EBADMSG;
173:     }
174: 
175:   if (vp_get32(buf + VP_OFF_CRC) != vp_crc32(buf, VP_RECORD_SIZE - 4))
176:     {
177:       return -EBADMSG;
178:     }
179: 
180:   flags    = vp_get16(buf + VP_OFF_FLAGS);
181:   ssid_len = buf[VP_OFF_SSID_LEN];
182:   psk_len  = buf[VP_OFF_PSK_LEN];
183: 
184:   if ((flags & ~(uint16_t)VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN) != 0)
185:     {
186:       return -EBADMSG;
187:     }
188: 
189:   if (ssid_len == 0 || ssid_len > VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX)
190:     {
191:       return -EBADMSG;
192:     }
193: 
194:   if (psk_len != 0 &&
195:       (psk_len < VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MIN || psk_len > VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX))
196:     {
197:       return -EBADMSG;
198:     }
199: 
200:   if (((flags & VP_RECORD_FLAG_OPEN) != 0) != (psk_len == 0))
201:     {
202:       return -EBADMSG;
203:     }
204: 
205:   if (!vp_padding_is_zero(buf, VP_OFF_SSID, ssid_len,
206:                           VELASIGHT_PROV_SSID_MAX) ||
207:       !vp_padding_is_zero(buf, VP_OFF_PSK, psk_len,
208:                           VELASIGHT_PROV_PSK_MAX))
209:     {
210:       return -EBADMSG;
211:     }
212: 
213:   memset(&parsed, 0, sizeof(parsed));
214:   memcpy(parsed.ssid, buf + VP_OFF_SSID, ssid_len);
215:   memcpy(parsed.password, buf + VP_OFF_PSK, psk_len);
216:   parsed.generation   = vp_get32(buf + VP_OFF_GEN);
217:   parsed.open_network = psk_len == 0;
218: 
219:   /* The record can be structurally perfect and still describe credentials the
220:    * running code would refuse, for instance after a limit changes.  Treat that
221:    * as corrupt rather than handing the caller something it cannot use.
222:    */
223: 
224:   if (vp_credentials_validate(&parsed) < 0)
225:     {
226:       return -EBADMSG;
227:     }

229:   *cred = parsed;

249:     }

251:   memcpy(dir, path, len);

263: {

266:   size_t dirlen;

286: int vp_store_save(const char *path,
287:                   const struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
288: {
289:   uint8_t record[VP_RECORD_SIZE];
290:   char tmp[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX + 16];
291:   FILE *stream;
292:   int ret;
293: 
294:   if (path == NULL || cred == NULL)
295:     {
296:       return -EINVAL;
297:     }
298: 
299:   if (strlen(path) >= VP_STORE_PATH_MAX)
300:     {
301:       return -ENAMETOOLONG;
302:     }
303: 
304:   ret = vp_record_encode(record, sizeof(record), cred);
305:   if (ret < 0)
306:     {
307:       return ret;
308:     }
309: 
310:   ret = vp_make_parent(path);
311:   if (ret < 0)
312:     {
313:       return ret;
314:     }
315: 
316:   ret = vp_store_temp_path(path, tmp, sizeof(tmp));
317:   if (ret < 0)
318:     {
319:       return ret;
320:     }
321: 
322:   stream = fopen(tmp, "wb");
323:   if (stream == NULL)
324:     {
325:       return -errno;
326:     }
327: 
328:   /* Write, flush, fsync, close, rename.  Without the fsync the rename can be
329:    * durable while the data behind it is not, which on a power cut leaves a
330:    * record that passes its own CRC check by accident or fails it for no
331:    * reason the next boot can explain.
332:    */
333: 
334:   if (fwrite(record, 1, sizeof(record), stream) != sizeof(record) ||
335:       fflush(stream) != 0 || fsync(fileno(stream)) != 0)
336:     {
337:       ret = errno != 0 ? -errno : -EIO;
338:       fclose(stream);
339:       unlink(tmp);
340:       return ret;
341:     }
342: 
343:   if (fclose(stream) != 0)
344:     {
345:       ret = errno != 0 ? -errno : -EIO;
346:       unlink(tmp);
347:       return ret;
348:     }
349: 
350:   if (rename(tmp, path) < 0)
351:     {
352:       ret = -errno;
353:       /* Keep a complete, fsynced scratch record.  FAT replacement unlinks an
354:        * existing destination before rename, so this may be the only valid
355:        * copy left after an interrupted replacement.  load() recovers it when
356:        * the final path is absent.
357:        */
358:       return ret;
359:     }
360: 
361:   sync();
362:   return 0;
363: }

365: int vp_store_load(const char *path,
366:                   struct velasight_prov_credentials_s *cred)
367: {
368:   uint8_t record[VP_RECORD_SIZE + 1];
369:   char tmp[VP_STORE_PATH_MAX + 16];
370:   FILE *stream;
371:   size_t nread;
372:   bool recover = false;
373: 
374:   if (path == NULL || cred == NULL)
375:     {
376:       return -EINVAL;
377:     }
378: 
379:   stream = fopen(path, "rb");
380:   if (stream == NULL)
381:     {
382:       /* ENOTDIR belongs with ENOENT here: a directory component that is
383:        * missing, or is a file, means nothing was ever stored.  NuttX's FAT
384:        * reports ENOTDIR for the missing-directory case where Linux reports
385:        * ENOENT, and a device that has simply never been provisioned should
386:        * not look like a broken one.  EINVAL is deliberately left alone: on
387:        * that filesystem it means the configured path cannot be represented,
388:        * which is a misconfiguration worth seeing.
389:        */
390: 
391:       if (errno == ENOENT || errno == ENOTDIR)
392:         {
393:           if (vp_store_temp_path(path, tmp, sizeof(tmp)) < 0)
394:             {
395:               return -ENOENT;
396:             }
397: 
398:           stream = fopen(tmp, "rb");
399:           if (stream == NULL)
400:             {
401:               return -ENOENT;
402:             }
403: 
404:           recover = true;
405:         }
406:       else
407:         {
408:           return -errno;
409:         }
410:     }
411: 
412:   nread = fread(record, 1, sizeof(record), stream);
413:   fclose(stream);
414: 
415:   if (vp_record_decode(record, nread, cred) < 0)
416:     {
417:       return -EBADMSG;
418:     }
419: 
420:   if (recover)
421:     {
422:       if (rename(tmp, path) < 0)
423:         {
424:           return -errno;
425:         }
426: 
427:       sync();
428:     }
429: 
430:   return 0;
431: }

**Findings**

High findings: none. Four medium correctness findings remain.

1. **Medium: the NAND readiness wait can expire before a valid configured initialization can finish.** `vs_config_wait_for_store()` waits only 7 seconds (`app/velasight/vs_config.c:20-31`). The board can delay initialization by up to 60 seconds, with a 5-second default (`board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/Kconfig:48-56`, scheduled at `board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:175-181`), and the subsequent MMCSD probe can itself wait another 7 seconds (`board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:25-26`, `board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:180-195`). Thus even the default timing can take roughly 12 seconds. If VelaSight times out first, `vs_network_open()` fails at `app/velasight/vs_network.c:218-225`; the app retains a null network handle and never retries, so neither STA nor provisioning AP is available for that boot.

2. **Medium: Kconfig permits VelaSight configurations in which its mandatory NAND backend can never become ready.** The VelaSight option only depends on framebuffer, buttons, and TCP (`app/velasight/Kconfig:1-10`), but `vs_config_wait_for_store()` unconditionally returns `-ENODEV` without `CONFIG_BK7258_SDIO` and waits forever-until-timeout if SDIO is enabled without automount (`app/velasight/vs_config.c:13-34`). There is no dependency on `BK7258_SDIO`, `BK7258_SDNAND_AUTOMOUNT`, or `FS_FAT`, even though the provisioning store defaults to VFAT-backed `/mnt/sdnand` (`app/provisioning_web/Kconfig:35-47`). Such configurations build successfully but always disable all VelaSight networking at runtime.

3. **Medium: scratch recovery masks real storage errors as “not provisioned” and can silently select the Kconfig credentials.** When the final record is absent, failure to open `vpsave.tmp` is always returned as `-ENOENT` at `app/provisioning_web/vp_store.c:398-402`, regardless of whether `fopen()` failed with `EIO`, `EACCES`, or another NAND/filesystem error. `vs_config_load_wifi()` treats `-ENOENT` as a clean first boot (`app/velasight/vs_config.c:67-80`) and then uses the Kconfig fallback (`app/velasight/vs_config.c:83-90`). A real scratch/NAND read failure can therefore make the device attempt the wrong network instead of reporting persistent-storage failure.

4. **Medium: a provisioning callback queued during manual AP exit is processed after the transition as if it still belonged to the current AP state.** The callback sets a persistent event flag at `app/velasight/vs_network.c:47-59`. AP-to-STA exit stops and joins the server but does not clear or consume that event (`app/velasight/vs_network.c:244-270`). Because the main loop checks callbacks before polling input (`app/velasight/vs_app.c:392-412`), a callback can arrive after that check and before a manual exit input is handled. On the next iteration, a stale failed-save event sets `VS_NET_AP_READY` at `app/velasight/vs_network.c:302-306` even though the mode is now STA, and the app moves back to the error page at `app/velasight/vs_app.c:397-402`. Clearing the AP generation’s pending event after the joined stop, or tagging events with an AP-session generation, is needed.

The previously targeted normal paths otherwise look addressed: failed saves leave the server available for another HTTP submission; ordinary AP-to-STA association/DHCP failures leave logical mode as STA so AP can be re-entered; close waits for provisioning shutdown before destroying the callback mutex; Make/CMake both expose the provisioning implementation; and VelaSight Wi-Fi no longer calls KVDB. The board KVDB loader’s Wi-Fi autostart is excluded for VelaSight at `board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:273-286`.
